classification.difficultyReason: Distinguish parameter interval length from angular coverage and assess whether changing one coordinate or the entire parameter reverses traversal, using counterexamples where needed.

content.prompt: True or False? The following statements are about the parametrisation of a circle.

children.label: a
children.prompt: The parametrisation $(\cos 2t,\sin 2t)$ for $0\leq t\leq\pi$ represents a semi-circle.

answer.short: False. It traces the whole unit circle.
answer.worked: As $t$ goes from $0$ to $\pi$, the angle $2t$ goes from $0$ to $2\pi$. The point completes one full revolution, tracing the whole unit circle.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If the domain is restricted, only a portion of the circle will be graphed.

answer.short: False. A restricted interval can cover the whole circle.
answer.worked: For $(\cos 6t,\sin 6t)$ with $0\leq t\leq\pi$, the angle $6t$ ranges from $0$ to $6\pi$. The point completes three full revolutions, tracing the entire circle.

children.label: c
children.prompt: If $(f(t),g(t))$ represents a circle going anti-clockwise, $(f(-t),g(t))$ represents a circle going clockwise.

answer.short: False. Changing $t$ in only one coordinate need not reverse the motion.
answer.worked: Take $f(t)=\cos t$ and $g(t)=\sin t$. Since $\cos(-t)=\cos t$, the new parametrisation remains $(\cos t,\sin t)$, which travels anti-clockwise as $t$ increases.

children.label: d
children.prompt: If $(f(t),g(t))$ represents a circle going anti-clockwise, $(f(-t),g(-t))$ represents a circle going clockwise.

answer.short: True. Replacing $t$ by $-t$ in both coordinates reverses the direction.
answer.worked: As $t$ increases, $-t$ decreases. Both coordinates therefore follow the original parametrisation in reverse order, so anti-clockwise motion becomes clockwise.
